sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Rotocasting Injection and Airbrush Finishing of Vinyl Art Collectibles

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg is also a member of the EU single market and applies EU trade and investment agreements and the EEA framework.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law), as amended by subsequent laws; Loi du 12 juillet 2013 portant création des sociétés en commandite spéciale (SCSp law); Implementing grand-ducal regulations; CSSF AML/CFT regulations and ESG guidelines issued under Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport or national identity card of each individual partner/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national ID issuing authority of the partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each individual partner/UBO (utility bill or bank reference not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, local authority, or regulated bank in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency / current corporate register excerpt for any corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate registrar of the corporate partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence for each non-resident partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the partner's tax residence country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration / UBO identification sheet in Luxembourg form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg formation agent, notary, or registered service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Luxembourg or signed before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Luxembourg formation agent and registered office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each partner or corporate partner's authorized representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, general partners, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, US OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg national PEP lists, FATF public statements, and international debarment databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, any high-risk third-country element, any complex ownership structure, or any unusual transaction profile. The screening must be refreshed before incorporation and annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may use the Latin alphabet. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Latin-script format for filing. The name must be available, non-confusing, truthful, and not contrary to public policy. For an SCSp, the name should include or be accompanied by the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' to indicate the limited liability partnership form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended at the LBR for a further 90-day period applied for before expiration. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Luxembourg Business Register within 30 days of rejection, after which the final refusal can be challenged before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in administrative proceedings, with the applicable statutory time limits and filing fees observed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally accepted for an SCSp registered office under Luxembourg law, provided a duly licensed Luxembourg corporate service provider or registered agent maintains the seat and administrative address. However, pure virtual or letterbox arrangements may be challenged where the entity engages in actual commercial operations such as manufacturing, warehousing, or direct retailing of designer toys; in such cases physical substance in Luxembourg must be demonstrable to satisfy the OECD substance requirements and Luxembourg tax residence/AEOI standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is 5% per operating year for a low-risk designer toy merchandising SCSp. The risk increases to a materially higher level if the entity is selected for FATF/EU high-risk sector screening, if transactions involve high-risk jurisdictions, or if the registered office provider is subject to regulatory inspection by the CSSF or RCS.

Legal drafting of SCSp partnership agreement and ancillary corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard SCSp formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for AML compliance under CSSF standards

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, specifically Part I, Articles 1-12 and the provisions on special limited partnerships introduced by the law of 23 July 2016 (société en commandite spéciale, SCSp); additionally, the law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Luxembourg District Court, operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Charter/Statuts) executed before a notary and filed for registration on the RCS via the eJustice / LBR online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital or positive net worth requirement; SCSp may set flexible contribution and capital account provisions in the limited partnership agreement. No escrow account is legally required; contribution obligations are contractual and may be deferred.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the founder-GP subscribes to and accepts the full partnership interest as set forth in the limited partnership agreement, with initial contribution to be recorded on the capital account; that the registered office be established at [address] in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; that the GP appoints the Managing Partner, [Name], to conduct day-to-day operations, represent the partnership before public authorities, and open bank accounts; that the RCS filing and publication formalities proceed; and that any ancillary matters be delegated to the GP, all effective as of this 1st day of [Month] [Year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and corporate name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS via eJustice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation application through the LBR online portal for the proposed SCSp denomination, including the required legal suffix 'SCSp'. Provide up to three alternative names and the intended corporate object. The procedure is electronic; no notarial deed is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Identity copies of the general partner and named officers
Power of attorney if a filing agent acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registered name, submission of a new name application with alternatives; a request may be made to the LBR for a reasoned rejection and a revised proposal filed within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp charter, including the registered office, duration, object, the identity of the general partner and the limited partner(s), contribution terms, management powers, profit/loss sharing, transfer rights, and the express designation of the law of Luxembourg as governing law. Present the deed before a Luxembourg notary for authentication; the notary physically verifies the identity of signatories and the legality of the clauses.
required_dossiers: Valid passports/IDs of all partners (GP and LPs)
Proof of professional address of the registered office
Statement of non-bankruptcy of the general partner (legal entity or natural person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions any clause, the parties may submit addenda or revised clauses to the notary and re-execute the deed; rejection notifications from the RCS are cured by filing clarifying resolutions or restated articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS electronic filing of the notarized charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the LBR e-filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized charter, the completed RCS registration form (Formulaire B), and supporting identity and address documents. Designate the beneficial owner for the UBO register in the same filing package. Pay the electronic filing fee. The RCS checks the completeness and legal compliance of the submission and assigns the RCS number.
required_dossiers: Consent of the general partner to serve as statutory manager if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query or a deficiency notice, the counsel must submit a corrective package (amended form, rectified charter or explanatory memorandum) within 15 days; re-filing may occur once the defect is remedied with no extra fine if filed within the statutory grace period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Luxembourg Official Gazette and legal effectiveness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mémorial B (Recueil des Sociétés et Associations) via LBR / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the official notice to the 'Mémorial B' for publication. The SCSp acquires legal personality once the RCS registration is completed; publication in the Mémorial serves as definitive opposability against third parties.
required_dossiers: Official notice text prepared by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, a request for rectification is submitted to the LBR; no judicial procedure is required for clerical corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of the manager and UBO declaration finalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the appointment of the managing partner (Gérant) through a written resolution. File or update the UBO register: identify each natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership. Submit identity details, address, and the nature and extent of the controlling interest. Obtain the RBE acknowledgement receipt.
required_dossiers: Management appointment resolution (if not in charter)
Supporting documentation for ownership percentage (partnership agreement or capital account statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE raises an inconsistency, provide a supplementary declaration and proof of the capital/ownership chain; a refusal is appealable to the RCS supervisory judge (justice de paix) as a first recourse.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) - Direction Générale de la Compétitivité, de l'Industrie et du Commerce
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Établissement classé (classified establishment permit) issued under the Luxembourg environmental permit law (loi modifiée du 10 juin 1999 relative aux établissements classés, now integrated into the law of 28 April 2022 on environmental permits)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (registration) – because plastic toy manufacturing by rotocasting, injection molding and airbrush finishing typically involves VOC emissions and limited chemical use; full EIA is not mandatory for small/medium production units, but a prescribed environmental compliance registration is required for volatile organic compound emissions above 1,000 kg per year.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emission threshold must not exceed the sectoral limit of 100 mg C/Nm3 for airbrush ovens; wastewater discharge must conform to general municipal pre-treatment limits (pH 6.5–9, COD < 1,000 mg/L, suspended solids < 400 mg/L, and no free cyanide); hazardous waste such as contaminated paints, thinners and cleaning rags must be stored separately, labelled and removed by a licensed waste carrier. Occupational air limits for toluene and methyl ethyl ketone follow EU indicative limit values; local exhaust ventilation and gas monitoring are required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate delivered by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) and the municipal fire prevention inspector; structural load inspection by an approved engineering bureau before occupation; and an occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering machine guards, spray booth electrical classification and worker exposure controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate and income tax matters; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration, filings and refunds; unified electronic portal: MyGuichet (https://guichet.public.lu); corporate registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (https://www.lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident sponsor establishing an SCSp: (1) execute the partnership deed before a Luxembourg notary; (2) file the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers to obtain the RCS registration and national matricule identification number; (3) submit the VAT registration application (inscription à la TVA) to the AEDT through MyGuichet, providing the partnership deed, RCS extract, proof of the designer-toy manufacturing and merchandising activity, and manager details; where the SCSp has no Luxembourg fixed establishment and is established outside the EU, it must appoint an approved VAT fiscal representative who is jointly and severally liable for Luxembourg VAT; (4) register the Luxembourg commercial establishment with the ACD for direct taxation and municipal business tax; (5) file the annual transparent partnership return and issue partner allocation statements reflecting each partner's distributable share. There is no minimum capital requirement, and 100% non-resident ownership is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; the SCSp is automatically fiscally transparent for corporate income tax, municipal business tax on the partners, and net wealth tax. Available statutory elections and mechanisms include: (i) VAT grouping election (assujettis unis) among Luxembourg-established taxable persons; (ii) the SCSp's separate status as a VAT taxable person where it independently carries on an economic activity; (iii) hybrid mismatch neutralisation elections under ATAD and ATAD 2 to align deduction and inclusion outcomes for transparent entities; and (iv) the vertical fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for qualifying corporate partners in respect of their allocable share of the transparent income. No election exists for entity-level CIT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold applies to non-resident taxable persons: any supplier making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must obtain an LU VAT number, except for the domestic small-enterprise exemption of EUR 35,000 annual turnover, which is reserved for Luxembourg-established businesses. Intra-EU distance sales of designer toys are reportable in Luxembourg under the Union OSS once the EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 is exceeded; non-EU sellers of B2C goods must register or use OSS/IOSS regardless of turnover. A valid EORI number is additionally required for export declarations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently has no real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory tax-authority API, or digital stamping regime. Structured e-invoicing (EN 16931) on the PEPPOL network is required for B2G invoicing to Luxembourg public entities. A domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate has been legislatively planned with effect from 1 January 2026, introducing structured e-invoices and periodic transaction-level reporting to the AEDT in alignment with the EU ViDA framework; until that date, PDF and paper invoices remain acceptable for B2B supplies and no continuous-control clearance obligation is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of designer blind-box toys to destinations outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 44(1)(1) of the Luxembourg VAT Act (implementing Article 146 of the EU VAT Directive) where: (i) the goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier or on his behalf beyond the EU customs territory; (ii) removal occurs within the statutory time frame, as a rule within 90 days of the time of supply; (iii) the supplier holds the customs export declaration and transport evidence in its name or that of its authorised agent; and (iv) the recipient is established outside the EU. The input VAT on related production costs, including vinyl compounds, rotocasting and injection materials, and airbrush finishing consumables, remains fully deductible against the zero-rated export revenue. Offshore services physically performed outside the EU may also be zero-rated where the respective statutory documentation is held.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Single Administrative Document / Export Accompanying Document bearing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) from the EU export system
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical removal of the goods from the EU customs territory to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the designer toy goods, quantities, unit values and INCO terms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT credit advice evidencing the collection of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer
Proof of exit, including border customs-office confirmation or destination-country customs arrival certificate
EORI number record and complete export dossier retention files covering the statutory retention period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is strictly audited by the AEDT under the adversarial tax-assessment procedure. Where the documentary bundle is incomplete, inconsistent or late, the exporter loses the export exemption, output VAT is reassessed at 17% on the invoice value, arrears interest accrues at 0.6% per month, and administrative increases are applied, typically 10% of the deficiency for negligence and up to 100% for deliberate concealment, in addition to per-invoice fines. The AEDT generally expects export proceeds to be received within 180 days of dispatch; unexplained open export receivables beyond that period increase audit risk and may trigger denial of the exemption. Fraudulent or circular export arrangements attract criminal tax-fraud prosecution with substantial monetary fines and imprisonment, extend the reassessment limitation period from 5 to 10 years, and render the VAT fiscal representative and managing partners jointly and severally liable for the clawed-back VAT, interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate foreign-exchange administration exists in Luxembourg; the BCL administers balance-of-payments statistics while the ECB retains monetary and reserve-management authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility: Luxembourg applies no exchange controls on current or capital-account transactions. Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital between Luxembourg, EU Member States and third countries. EUR is the sole legal tender, but multi-currency accounts (USD, GBP, CNH) are freely permitted. No prior BCL or CSSF authorisation is required for inbound equity into an SCSp, for operational outflows, or for profit remittance. The pass-through SCSp is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax; non-resident partner withdrawals are unrestricted at banking level and are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax. The only practical hurdle is mandatory statistical balance-of-payments reporting by the bank and, for direct-investment positions, by the SCSp itself.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no minimum conversion ratio, and no foreign-currency retention limits. Exporters may hold 100% of proceeds in any currency, domestically or abroad. The sole compliance requirement is statistical: payment-service providers must report cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 to the BCL via the LuxGBP reporting system; direct-investment capital flows and outstanding positions must be reported under BCL Circular 2009/02 where thresholds are met.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account (multi-currency EUR/USD/CNH), trade-finance facility and commercial LC desk
Capital escrow account (compte séquestre) for committed partner contributions; operational current account opened alongside
Operational MT103 clearing account with documentary credit (UCP 600), BPO and RMB-corridor settlement capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BCEE (Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État - Spuerkees)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EUR operational account with segregated merchant-settlement sub-accounts for e-commerce treasury
Wholesale transaction account for liquidity concentration, MT103 settlements and daily sweeping
Operational account for FX-forward margining and short-term working-capital flows
CNH (offshore renminbi) clearing and settlement account for Chinese manufacturer payouts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: HIGH as a secondary treasury and payment rail; LOW as the sole primary banking relationship for an SCSp. Legal constraints: any e-money institution (EMI) serving the SCSp must hold a valid licence under Directive 2009/110/EC in an EEA state and be passported into Luxembourg via the CSSF notification mechanism under PSD2 (Law of 10 November 2009, as amended). EMI client funds are safeguarded by segregation or insurance but are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL); balances above EUR 100,000 should be swept daily to a credit institution. EMIs cannot grant loans, overdraft facilities, or issue commercial letters of credit. Recommended provider stack: Stripe (Stripe Technology Europe Ltd, passported from Ireland) for Shopify Payments and online card acquiring; Airwallex or Ebury for multi-currency global accounts, low-value FX conversion, and supplier payouts; Mangopay (CSSF-licensed Luxembourg EMI) for marketplace split payments if a reseller platform is added. Primary bank clearing should remain with BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, or BCEE.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence interview is effectively mandatory for first-time onboarding of an SCSp with non-EU beneficial owners. A representative of the general partner (associé gérant) or the UBO must attend one in-person due-diligence meeting at the bank's Luxembourg premises with original passport and proof-of-address documents. Remote video-KYC is available at BIL and BGL BNP Paribas for EU-resident UBOs, subject to CSSF Circular 19-716 expectations, with notarised and apostilled documentary packages. The mandatory dossier consists of the limited partnership agreement (LPA), a current extract from the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), signed powers of attorney, certified copies of the general partner's corporate documents, six months of bank statements for funding partners, and a concise business plan describing the designer blind-box toy manufacturing and merchandising model. A scheduled week-long Luxembourg visit is strongly recommended to close the account within two to three weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp opacity: the partnership is not automatically registered in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), so the bank cannot independently verify partners or the economic ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised private deed or LPA, current partner and capital-commitment schedule, RBE beneficial-ownership extract, Luxembourg counsel legal opinion confirming existence, capacity and signature authority of the SCSp, and a notarised power of attorney of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification mismatch: the bank may flag the SCSp as an opaque financial entity or treated fund, creating withholding and reporting confusion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed self-certification of the SCSp as an Active Non-Financial Entity (NFE) because its gross income derives from active manufacturing and sale of goods (ISIC 3240) rather than financial investment; Form W-8BEN-E for each US partner; CRS documentation of all partners; and a legal note confirming income-tax pass-through under Luxembourg tax law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentrated cross-border payments to Chinese vinyl-toy manufacturers may be screen-tested for trade-based money laundering or sanctions evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master manufacturing agreements, confirmed purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations (HS 9503), bill-of-lading or waybill copies, EU/OFAX screening reports for all counterparties, and an arm's-length pricing memorandum supporting supplier payment values.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue arriving from Shopify Payments and Stripe without bank-level KYC on end consumers generates opaque revenue flow in the AML officer's review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid merchant service agreements with Shopify Payments and Stripe, PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication compliance attestation, API-generated transaction-level settlements and reconciliation exports, platform-level KYC verification evidence, and a narrated description of the blind-box online retail model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth ambiguity for non-resident founding partners injecting the initial SCSp capital from foreign jurisdictions or mixed private-asset portfolios.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of certified bank statements from each contributing partner, tax-residency certificates, a signed source-of-wealth affidavit with supporting asset-sale or employment documents, capital-call resolutions executed by the general partner, and confirmation that no proceeds derive from unlicensed investment activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) partners send SWIFT MT103 wires, never cash, to the SCSp's LU-format IBAN at BGL BNP Paribas or BIL with beneficiary name matching the RBE-registered legal name; (2) remittance reference must cite the capital-call notice number, partner identification, and BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment-equity in a Luxembourg special limited partnership; (3) any transfer equal to or above EUR 100,000 requires pre-notification to the bank's compliance desk together with the signed capital-call resolution, the LPA extract, and the source-of-funds file; (4) no BCL or Ministry of Finance authorisation is required for inbound capital under EU free-movement-of-capital rules; (5) US-sourced capital must be supported by the investor's FBAR and IRS Form 8938 compliance evidence and the SCSp's FATCA Chapter 4 classification; (6) the receiving account must be contractually identified as the contribution account in the LPA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to offshore suppliers (PRC vinyl injection factories) use: (i) SWIFT MT103 for routine open-account payments in EUR or USD, citing the invoice number, Incoterms, and the description 'ISIC 3240 plastic art collectibles' on the wire instruction; (ii) irrevocable confirmed commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 issued by BGL BNP Paribas or BIL trade finance desks for first-time or large purchase orders, advised through Bank of China or ICBC; (iii) direct CNH renminbi remittances via the Luxembourg RMB clearing centre (Bank of China Europe S.A. as clearing bank) when Chinese suppliers require RMB settlement; (iv) card and small-value operating disbursements via the approved EMI rails (Airwallex, Wise) for subscriptions, marketing, and logistics fees. Every outbound payment must be matched to a signed goods or services contract and an underlying invoice to withstand bank UBO and shipping-chain review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or local master agreement with BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, or Société Générale Luxembourg
EUR/CNH and USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), fixed against offshore RMB reference rates, permitted for the SCSp as a non-financial counterparty below the EMIR clearing threshold
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and USD/CNH) to match USD e-commerce revenue against USD material purchases from Chinese manufacturers
Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars to manage EUR/USD conversion volatility on Shopify Payments and Stripe settlements

CNH forward swaps executed through the Luxembourg RMB clearing pool, documented as hedging-only instruments and requiring prior written approval of the general partner under the SCSp risk-management policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE annual validation), including updated ownership information for any share/interest transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), operated with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/Greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: filed within one calendar month after each anniversary of the RBE registration; updated declaration due within one month of any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing exposes the SCSp and its general partner to criminal fines from EUR 125 to EUR 5,000; repeated non-submission may trigger official reprimand, publication of the breach, blocking of partner distributions and administrative strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and annex (comptes annuels) filing with the commercial register, where applicable for the SCSp (mandatory only for non-exempt or regulated entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file gives rise to a court order to file, administrative fines up to EUR 750, potential criminal liability of directors/general partners, adverse credit information and, in persistent cases, judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct-tax declaration for the fiscally transparent SCSp (partnership income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; timely electronic filing can obtain an administrative extension to 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers monthly interest of 0.6%, a default surcharge of up to 10% and reassessment of taxable income; wilful non-filing carries criminal tax penalties. The tax default does not directly cause strike-off but may lead to enforced recovery against the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic independent audit for an unregulated SCSp. If a statutory audit threshold is triggered (for corporate entities generally: exceeding two of three criteria of balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million and 50 average employees) or if the SCSp is a regulated alternative investment fund (CSSF-authorised SIF, SICAR or AIFM fund), the SCSp must appoint an approved Luxembourg statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Default accounting framework is Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the Law of 19 December 2002 on accounting and annual accounts. Regulated SCSPs or fund vehicles may apply IFRS or CSSF-specific presentation rules where contractually or regulatorily required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent or general partner must verify the identity of each ultimate beneficial owner, collect any updated ownership documentation and submit the annual RBE confirmation before the statutory anniversary deadline. Any change in partners or transfer of partnership interests must be filed within one month of the change; the annual confirmation must then reflect such updated data and is not deferred to the usual anniversary cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members/Partners (SCSp interest register reflecting general and limited partners)
Register of Directors/Managers and partners' written resolutions
Minute book of partners' meetings and GP decisions
Register of transfers of partnership interests and capital calls/distributions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 - USD 5,500 per year for registered office, corporate agent and annual RBE/regulatory filing services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per year if a statutory or contractual audit is required; nil for an exempt, unregulated SCSp.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg applies a combined corporate income tax rate of 24.94% (17% CIT plus 7% municipal business tax surcharge on the CIT base, plus 0.7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT base). An SCSp is treated as a fiscally transparent partnership for Luxembourg income tax purposes unless it opts for corporate taxation; therefore, profits are generally taxed at the partner level. Specific incentives include the IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective rate of 5.16%), the R&D tax credit (25% of eligible R&D expenditures, for small companies), and the investment tax credit for additional investments of up to 13.5% with a 50% cap for small and medium enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 6 (Fiches impôts et déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (Guichet.lu eCDF – electronic Corporate Declaration Filing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions may be granted by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) upon request. For an SCSp, the return is filed by the tax representative or the managing partner; unless the partnership opts for corporate taxation, the return reports the allocated share of income to each partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp: entity name, RCS registration number (Luxembourg Business Registers), fiscal year, and legal form code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide their foreign tax identification number, country of tax residence, and permanent address; a Luxembourg tax representative (impôt representative) must be appointed for non-resident partners without a Luxembourg establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of commercial net result: turnover, cost of goods sold (including costs of raw materials for vinyl rotocasting, resin, and paint), operating expenses, depreciation, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income and expenses attributable to the Luxembourg SCSp must be declared on a worldwide basis for the partnership, with territorial allocation for permanent establishments situated abroad; non-resident partners report their distributive share in their residence jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegration of non-deductible expenses and application of tax-exempt income, including adjustments for transfer pricing adjustments, thin capitalization, and IP box exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure that any intercompany transactions are priced at arm's length; no automatic deduction is available for expenses incurred in a non-cooperative jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base and allocable share to each partner (for a transparent SCSp, each partner is separately assessed on their pro-rata share).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must attach a statement of their share, including any withholding tax credit or exemption claim under Luxembourg domestic law or applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) base and determination of solidarity surcharge allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For transparent partnerships, the municipal business tax is assessed on the partnership in certain circumstances where a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists; non-resident partners are exempt from municipal business tax on their share unless attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: administrative fine up to EUR 3,000 per required return; additional tax assessments based on best judgment (taxation d'office) can be issued. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) on unpaid corporate income tax. Willful non-filing or fraudulent filing may trigger criminal penalties for tax evasion (Articles 398–401 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law), including imprisonment for up to one year and fines up to EUR 50,000 per infraction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on Luxembourg-source dividend distributions, the recipient must be the legal and beneficial owner of the income and submit a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (Form 13 or attestation from the foreign tax authority) to the paying agent before payment. For outbound dividends paid by an SCSp that has opted to be treated as a transparent entity, withholding tax is generally not levied at partnership level; instead, income is allocated to partners. Where a non-resident partner receives a distribution that is characterized as a dividend from a Luxembourg subsidiary (e.g., if the SCSp is treated as a corporation), the reduced DTA rate must be applied for by completing a standard application for partial or full exemption (Form 13), attaching the foreign tax authority residence certificate and a copy of the underlying audited financial statements. The Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) must approve the relief before or at the time of distribution if the taxpayer elects to avoid the full 15% statutory rate. Parent-subsidiary directive relief (0%) applies to EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months, subject to anti-abuse rules under ATAD.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties: 0% (Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on royalty payments, including patent and trademark royalties, unless the payment is assimilated to hidden profit distribution to a non-resident shareholder). Treaty rates for royalties under Luxembourg DTAs vary from 0% to 10%, with most OECD-compliant treaties providing 5% or 0% for beneficial owners. Statutory withholding tax on interest: 0% (no domestic withholding tax on interest, except for interest treated as constructive dividend or connected to certain profit-participating loans). Treaty rates on interest: 0% under most Luxembourg DTAs. An exemption from net wealth tax may apply to receivables, but the 15% withholding tax on dividends remains relevant for profit distributions from a corporate-treated entity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 0 (no statutory monetary threshold for preparing transfer pricing documentation; all intercompany transactions must be documented on an arm's length basis under OECD TP Guidelines; Master File and Local File thresholds under Luxembourg law follow EU TP documentation requirements and apply to multinational groups with consolidated revenues above EUR 750 million, subject to country-by-country reporting obligations; for local file preparation, the ACD requires documentation for any cross-border related party transaction regardless of amount, and penalties may apply for incomplete TP documentation).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies substance requirements through domestic law principles and anti-abuse doctrines. The Tax Administration may disregard an SCSp or its transactions if the arrangement is artificial or lacks economic substance. Since 1 January 2019, Luxembourg applies a general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) pursuant to the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD). Economic Substance Regulations in the strict sense (ESR as in UAE/offshore regimes) do not exist in Luxembourg, but the substance-over-form doctrine and the judicial principle of 'fictitious transactions' allow the tax authorities to recharacterize a shell-like SCSp. The following substance indicia are required to obtain treaty benefits and protect against BEPS assertions: the SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg registered office, hold board meetings or partner meetings, maintain a Luxembourg bank account, employ qualified administrative staff (at least part-time), ensure the managing general partner (SCSc or S.à r.l.) exercises genuine management functions, record commercial contracts, and demonstrate an actual decision-making structure commensurate with the activity (designer toy design, procurement of vinyl or resin materials, quality control, and distribution). Failure to demonstrate substance may result in denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of profits on a look-through basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable revenue from online sales of designer blind box toys via Shopify, Stripe or local POS, without recording cash transactions, issuing false invoices, under-declaring e-commerce turnover, or using undisclosed foreign bank accounts. Also includes the intentional failure to register as a taxable person for VAT and CIT, or knowingly filing a false tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 396 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and a fine of EUR 5,000 to EUR 20,000 (doubled to EUR 100,000 for serious cases under Article 398). The fine may be multiplied up to ten times when the evasion amounts exceed EUR 10,000. Additionally, the taxpayer must pay all evaded taxes plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner of the SCSp can be held jointly and severally liable for the partnership's tax debts under Luxembourg fiscal law and general civil law (Article 1837 of the Luxembourg Civil Code). If the managing partner acts in bad faith or gross negligence, the corporate veil may be pierced. Directors face criminal fines and imprisonment, civil restitution of all evaded taxes, and possible travel bans or reporting obligations imposed by the Luxembourg criminal courts. The general partner of an SCSp is personally, jointly and severally liable for all partnership obligations if the partnership is insolvent and the director participated in fraudulent transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox entity with no Luxembourg administration, no local bank account, no actual management of the designer toy business, no employees or leasing of office premises, and no genuine economic activity in Luxembourg, while claiming Luxembourg residence and treaty benefits on passive income or e-commerce royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg GAAR (Article 6 Bofisc) and ATAD GAAR allow the tax authorities to disregard the entity for tax purposes. The business profits are reallocated to the actual shareholders or to a deemed permanent establishment in the market jurisdiction. The 15% withholding tax or higher may be applied to a deemed distribution, and net wealth tax and municipal business tax are reassessed. No specific monetary fine applies to the shell company itself, but an administrative penalty for false attestation of substance can reach EUR 4,000 per infraction under the Luxembourg tax procedure, and full tax reassessment plus 0.6% monthly interest is imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false substance documents face personal criminal liability for complicity in tax evasion (Article 397 of the General Tax Law) and may be fined up to EUR 20,000 and imprisoned. In civil proceedings, the director or general partner may be ordered by a tribunal to compensate the tax administration and creditors. A travel ban can be issued by an investigating judge in case of serious fiscal fraud, and directors cannot leave the Grand Duchy without court authorization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using anonymous or unregistered payment structures for the designer blind box toy e-commerce business, accepting large cash payments without identification despite the low-risk tier, failing to register with the Luxembourg Register of Effective Beneficial Owners (RBE), failing to file the annual beneficial ownership declaration, or processing payments through shell PSP accounts without proper KYC in a way that obscures the economic reality of transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, failure to comply with beneficial ownership registration (law of 13 January 2019) is punishable by a fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons, plus administrative fines from the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) up to EUR 1 million or 10% of turnover. Criminal penalties for money laundering can reach 5 years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 500,000 for natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly process proceeds of tax evasion face criminal liability for money laundering (Article 506-1 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code). Liability extends to the general partner of the SCSp; any director or manager who obstructs the RBE filing may be personally fined up to EUR 125,000 and banned from managing a commercial company for up to 10 years. Asset freezing orders and travel bans are applicable during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Missing VAT / E-Commerce Registration (Luxembourg and EU)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to charge Luxembourg VAT on taxable B2C sales of designer blind box toys, failing to register for the One-Stop Shop (OSS) for distance sales, exceeding the EUR 10,000 EU-wide cross-border threshold without registering, or not filing periodic recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) for B2B supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg VAT law (loi modifiée du 12 février 1979) imposes a surcharge of 10% of the VAT due for late filing; a further EUR 1,250 penalty for late declaration may apply. If the tax administration discovers undeclared output VAT, an additional penalty of 5% per month up to 25% of the due amount is imposed. Intention to evade VAT triggers the same criminal sanctions as tax evasion: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to EUR 20,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner or director who signs false VAT returns is a joint and several debtor of the VAT liability of the entity (Article 56 of the Luxembourg VAT law). Repetition of customs-like or intra-community fraud can lead to personal liability. Travel bans and director disqualification can be ordered upon indictment, and the personal property of directors can be seized for the VAT debts if the company is insolvent and the non-filing was a management fault.
